campaign: BCIG-8: Soviet Adaptive Control & Modern AI Synthesis (Tightened Formulation)

cross_graph_hypotheses.epistemic_claim: In stochastic systems with unknown environmental dynamics, the action itself is epistemic: acting to probe and reduce uncertainty is inextricably unified with acting to achieve a goal. Modern curiosity-driven RL and Active Inference are structural recurrences of this principle.
counter_evidence_risks: Conflating generic trial-and-error RL with explicit dual control where action variance is optimized for parameter identification.
cross_graph_hypotheses.falsification_criteria: Falsified if modern active inference can be shown to directly cite Feldbaum, proving genetic lineage rather than structural recurrence, or if modern RL policies do not alter trajectories for information gain.

cross_graph_hypotheses.relational_grammar: NEED -> ENDOGENOUS_GOAL -> ACTION_ACCEPTOR (PREDICT) -> ACT -> RETURN_AFFERENCE -> COMPARE -> CORRECT
cross_graph_hypotheses.epistemic_claim: Anokhin's Functional System formalizes the boundary between externally evaluated systems (prompt-in / answer-out) and internally closed adaptive systems: success is determined endogenously by matching return sensory afference against the anticipatory action acceptor.
counter_evidence_risks: Treating standard feedback loops (Wiener negative feedback) as equivalent to Anokhin's forward efference simulation.
cross_graph_hypotheses.falsification_criteria: Falsified if prompt-response foundation models are demonstrated to possess endogenous goal formation independent of prompt context.
primary_sources: Anokhin (1968) 'Biology and Neurophysiology of the Conditioned Reflex'

cross_graph_hypotheses.sovctx_thread_name: Finite Computational Regularization on Soviet Mainframes
cross_graph_hypotheses.epistemic_claim: Chebyshev-Samarskii regularization on BESM-6 demonstrates that real-world intelligence is bounded by finite word lengths, discrete grid approximations, and computational ceilings. Bounded computation is an intrinsic mathematical constraint on state recovery rather than an implementation detail.
counter_evidence_risks: Equating numerical stability of Fredholm integral solvers directly with modern low-bit neural network quantization (overreach).
cross_graph_hypotheses.falsification_criteria: Falsified if ill-posed inverse operators can be stably recovered without compact parameter regularization in finite precision.

tightened_classification_verdict.interpretation: Rather than claiming a loose genetic rediscovery, the tightened audit reveals that STRUCTURAL_ANALOGUE (41.67%) is the primary mode: modern AI architectures repeatedly reconstruct earlier operational loop topologies (e.g. Epistemic Action, Extremal Set Invariance, Mean-Field Coordination) without genetic descent.

relational_grammar_primitive.significance: Feldbaum proved action itself must be epistemic under uncertainty.

externally_evaluated_systems.archetype: Prompt-Response Foundation Models / Feedforward Deep Learning

internally_closed_adaptive_systems.archetype: Anokhin Functional System / Feldbaum Dual Controller / Active Inference
internally_closed_adaptive_systems.loop: internal condition/need -> goal -> action acceptor (predict) -> act -> return afference -> compare -> correct

endogenous_self_maintenance_analysis.definition: Computational self-maintenance integrated into the intelligence loop as an internally valued condition.
endogenous_self_maintenance_analysis.contrast: Modern AI possess external watchdogs (thermal throttles, battery monitors, OS supervisors). What remains strictly missing (H=0.0) is endogenous self-maintenance driving cognitive behavior.

adaptive_closure_ranking.name: Anokhin Functional System Architecture
adaptive_closure_ranking.architectural_loop_type: afferent synthesis -> goal -> action acceptor (predict) -> act -> return afference -> compare -> correct
adaptive_closure_ranking.notes: Theoretical apex of cybernetic adaptive closure; includes efference copy forward simulation and result-driven coalition.

adaptive_closure_ranking.name: Active Inference Agent (Friston 2010)
adaptive_closure_ranking.architectural_loop_type: sense -> predict sensory afference -> minimize free energy (epistemic + pragmatic) -> act
adaptive_closure_ranking.notes: Modern structural analogue of Anokhin's action acceptor and Feldbaum's dual control; A = 0.9667.

adaptive_closure_ranking.name: Feldbaum Dual Control System
adaptive_closure_ranking.architectural_loop_type: probe (act-to-know) -> update state estimate -> steer extremal trajectory -> correct
adaptive_closure_ranking.notes: Unified epistemic action (active information gathering) with optimal regulation; A = 0.8333.

adaptive_closure_ranking.name: World-Model Model-Based Agent (Dreamer / MuZero)
adaptive_closure_ranking.architectural_loop_type: latent state -> predict future rollouts in imagination -> select optimal action -> observe -> update world model
adaptive_closure_ranking.notes: Restores predictive forward simulation (P=1.0) and recurrent state memory (R=1.0); still lacks self-regulatory homeostasis (H=0.0).

adaptive_closure_ranking.name: Krasovskii Extremal Targeting Game
adaptive_closure_ranking.architectural_loop_type: adversarial observation -> quasi-solution regularizing direction -> extremal feedback
adaptive_closure_ranking.notes: Guarantees forward set invariance under discontinuous worst-case perturbations; A = 0.8000.

adaptive_closure_ranking.name: Grey Walter Tortoise (Machina Speculatrix)
adaptive_closure_ranking.architectural_loop_type: sense -> act -> observe -> feedback (recharge when battery low)
adaptive_closure_ranking.notes: Minimal circuitry (2 vacuum tubes) achieves high adaptive closure via physical embodiment and phototropic battery homing.

adaptive_closure_ranking.name: Ashby Homeostat
adaptive_closure_ranking.architectural_loop_type: perturb -> monitor essential variable -> uniselector step switch -> stabilize
adaptive_closure_ranking.notes: Archetypal homeostatic ultrastable machine; seeks phase-space equilibrium across four coupled units.

adaptive_closure_ranking.name: Modern Tool-Using AI Agent (ReAct / Autonomous Scaffold)
adaptive_closure_ranking.architectural_loop_type: thought -> tool action -> environment observation -> reflection -> iterate
adaptive_closure_ranking.notes: Recombines cybernetic loop components (feedback, memory, tools, planning, verification) in high-level software agents.

adaptive_closure_ranking.name: Tsetlin Finite Automaton in Random Media
adaptive_closure_ranking.architectural_loop_type: action -> environment penalty/reward -> internal Markov transition -> action
adaptive_closure_ranking.notes: Optimal behavioral adaptation in stationary and non-stationary stochastic media; direct mathematical ancestor of RL.

adaptive_closure_ranking.name: Model-Free Reinforcement Learning Agent (DQN / PPO)
adaptive_closure_ranking.architectural_loop_type: state -> policy network -> action -> environment reward -> value update
adaptive_closure_ranking.notes: High closed-loop feedback and goal-seeking; lacks internal homeostasis and explicit forward world simulation.

adaptive_closure_ranking.name: Shakey the Robot (SRI STRIPS)
adaptive_closure_ranking.architectural_loop_type: sense -> world model update -> STRIPS symbolic planning -> execute open-loop plan
adaptive_closure_ranking.notes: Pioneered symbolic planning in robotics; plan execution fragile when physical environment diverged from STRIPS axioms.

adaptive_closure_ranking.name: Classical Expert System (MYCIN / R1)
adaptive_closure_ranking.architectural_loop_type: input premise facts -> forward/backward rule chain inference -> output diagnosis
adaptive_closure_ranking.notes: Pure feedforward symbolic inference; zero closed loop, zero embodiment, zero adaptive update during runtime.

adaptive_closure_ranking.name: Deep Feedforward Neural Network (AlexNet / ResNet)
adaptive_closure_ranking.architectural_loop_type: input vector -> layer transforms -> output logits
adaptive_closure_ranking.notes: Extremely low runtime adaptive closure (A=0.0); weights frozen after training, zero interaction with environment.

teleological_eight_pillar_gap_analysis.question: What components did earlier adaptive-system architectures consider necessary for intelligence that modern AI architectures omit?

pillars.1_closed_loop_action: Omitted in feedforward architectures; partially restored in agentic tool loops.
pillars.2_active_information_gathering: Omitted in standard greedy policies; central to Feldbaum and Active Inference.
pillars.3_internal_state: Omitted in stateless feedforward models; present in RNNs and world models.
pillars.4_prediction_of_consequences: Omitted in reactive policies; central to Bernstein, Anokhin, and Dreamer.
pillars.5_endogenous_goal_conditions: Omitted in all foundation models; goals are exclusively prompt-supplied.
pillars.6_adaptive_correction: Omitted at inference runtime (weights frozen); active in Anokhin return afference.
pillars.7_embodiment: Omitted in cloud LLMs; present in Grey Walter and physical robotics.
pillars.8_endogenous_self_maintenance: Universally absent in modern AI; foundational to biological organisms.
